description: CREATES an AI image story: a narrated script turned into a sequence of AI-generated images, read aloud with captions over it. Suited to facts, history, horror, storytime and explainers. YOU WRITE THE SCRIPT, AND ONLY THE SCRIPT: the `text` you send is the narration that is spoken, verbatim, in that order (`get_recipe` `image-story` has the writing advice and a worked example). Show it to the user as plain text before spending anything and change it until they like it (iterating is free). Never write the pictures: aicut cuts your script into scenes and writes every image prompt itself. PRICE IS DRIVEN BY THE IMAGE COUNT, not the words: `estimate_only: true` returns `scene_count` and `voice_provider` beside the money, so say the count and the price. The levers: `seconds_per_image` (3 default; 5 is cheaper, 2 dearer), `image_model` (`zit-realism` is the cheap default; `gpt-image-2.5` costs noticeably more per image: offer it only when asked and quote it first) and `voice_provider` (ElevenLabs costs more per character than openai). Re-quote after changing any of them or adding a `style_id` (`list_image_story_styles`: it forces the expensive edit-capable image model). AFTER: this one call makes the finished video (the answer carries `scene_count`, the price split and `renders_automatically: true`; no fire or render step). Wait with `wait_for_generation`; when terminal `get_video` carries the file url. `start_confirmed: false` means the job exists but its start was never confirmed: do not create it again, watch it, and tell the user it may need a retry if it has not moved in fifteen minutes. LANGUAGE: a script not in `language` is TRANSLATED, so a quote is exact only for the script you sent. A script over the language's character limit is refused (aicut will NOT cut it); too many images for one video: use a longer `seconds_per_image`. SPENDS TOKENS: price with `estimate_only: true`, ask in the SAME message as the price, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase (SPENDING RULES, this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: a reused `idempotency_key` REPLAYS the first job whatever the settings: never reuse one for a new generation (this server's instructions).

aspect_ratio.description: Defaults to `9:16`, the vertical shape every short-form platform wants.

caption_style.description: How the burned-in captions look; default `karaoke`; `none` turns them off.

image_model.description: The look of the images; default `zit-realism` (photoreal, cheapest). `zit-lora-*` and `zit-comic` are illustrated looks at the same price, `flux-klein*` cost more, `gpt-image-2.5` is the priciest: quote it before you pick it.

image_resolution.description: Defaults to `standard`. `high` selects the model's high-resolution price row (for some models both rows cost the same).

language.description: The language `text` is written in, by name; default English. Naming another language makes aicut translate the script, which changes its length and the price.

seconds_per_image.description: How long each image stays on screen; default 3. THE MAIN PRICE LEVER: 5 buys roughly 40% fewer images than 3 for the same script, 2 buys 50% more.

sound_effects.description: An ambient sound effect per scene. Defaults to false, and it ADDS to the price by the video's length: quote it.

style_id.description: An authored look from `list_image_story_styles`. It forces the expensive edit-capable image model, so re-quote. Omit for aicut's default photorealistic look.

text.description: The narration script in plain prose: what the voice says, start to finish. No scene markers, image directions or speaker labels; aicut cuts it into scenes and writes every image itself.

transition_effects.description: A visual slide between scenes. Defaults to false; free.

transition_sounds.description: A whoosh between scenes. Defaults to false; free.

voice.description: The narrator's voice. The voice id, in the provider named by `voice_provider`; omit for that provider's default narrator. openai: alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse (`ash` reads deepest, `shimmer` and `sage` lighter; retired `onyx`, `nova`, `fable` still work, speaking as `ash`, `shimmer`, `alloy`). elevenlabs: an id from `list_voices` with `provider: 'elevenlabs'` (stock, cloned or custom voices; PAGED: pass `limit: 100` and read `has_more` before saying a voice does not exist). Any other id is refused uncharged. Cloned and custom ElevenLabs voices ARE accepted here and on `generate_fake_text_video`; `generate_audio` cannot.

voice_provider.description: Which voice service reads the narration. `elevenlabs` is the web app's default, `openai` is cheaper and covers every language with the same eight voices. Defaults to `openai`. IT CHANGES THE PRICE: ElevenLabs costs about four times openai per character, so call `estimate_only` again after changing it.
